description: Comprehensive 50-Question Physics Question Bank for Diffraction Grating Spectrometry

questions.question: What is the standard grating equation for normal incident light?
questions.answer: d · sin(θ) = m · λ
questions.correct_option: d · sin(θ) = m · λ
questions.explanation: For normal incidence, constructive interference from adjacent slits occurs when the path difference d sin(θ) equals an integer multiple of the wavelength mλ.

questions.question: In the grating equation d · sin(θ) = m · λ, what does 'd' represent?
options: The distance between centers of adjacent slits (grating pitch)
The total width of the grating plate
The distance from the grating to the screen
The diameter of the laser beam spot
questions.answer: The distance between centers of adjacent slits (grating pitch)
questions.correct_option: The distance between centers of adjacent slits (grating pitch)
questions.explanation: The grating element d represents the slit separation (pitch), calculated as d = 1 / N where N is the line density.

questions.question: If a diffraction grating has 500 lines per mm, what is its slit spacing d?
What diffraction order corresponds to the undeflected central beam (θ = 0)?
questions.answer: Zeroth order (m = 0)
questions.correct_option: Zeroth order (m = 0)
questions.explanation: At θ = 0, path difference between all slits is zero regardless of wavelength, corresponding to the central m = 0 maximum.

questions.question: When white light is incident on a diffraction grating, what color is the central maximum (m = 0)?
questions.answer: White
questions.correct_option: White
questions.explanation: All visible wavelengths satisfy d sin(0) = 0 · λ at θ = 0, so all spectral colors recombine into an undiffracted white fringe.

questions.question: In the first-order spectrum (m = 1), which color of visible light diffracts at the largest angle θ?
questions.answer: Red (~650 nm)
questions.correct_option: Red (~650 nm)
questions.explanation: Since sin(θ) = mλ / d, angle θ increases monotonically with wavelength λ. Red light has the longest visible wavelength and diffracts furthest.

questions.question: How does spectral dispersion by a diffraction grating compare to dispersion by a glass prism?
options: Grating bends red more than violet; prism bends violet more than red
Both bend red light more than violet light
Both bend violet light more than red light
questions.answer: Grating bends red more than violet; prism bends violet more than red
questions.correct_option: Grating bends red more than violet; prism bends violet more than red
questions.explanation: In a grating, sin(θ) ∝ λ (red deflects most). In a prism, refractive index n increases for shorter wavelengths, bending violet most.

questions.question: What is the theoretical maximum observable order m_max for light of wavelength λ with grating spacing d?
questions.answer: m_max = ⌊d / λ⌋
questions.correct_option: m_max = ⌊d / λ⌋
questions.explanation: Because sin(θ) cannot exceed 1, mλ / d ≤ 1 ⟹ m ≤ d / λ. The highest integer order is ⌊d / λ⌋.

questions.question: What happens to the angular separation between diffracted lines if a 300 lines/mm grating is replaced with a 600 lines/mm grating?
questions.answer: Angular separation doubles (spreads further apart)
questions.correct_option: Angular separation doubles (spreads further apart)
questions.explanation: Doubling ruling density halves slit spacing d. Because sin(θ) = mλ / d, smaller d results in significantly larger diffraction angles.

questions.question: Angular dispersion D of a diffraction grating is mathematically defined as:
options: D = dθ / dλ = m / (d · cos θ)
D = dλ / dθ = (d · sin θ) / m
questions.answer: D = dθ / dλ = m / (d · cos θ)
questions.correct_option: D = dθ / dλ = m / (d · cos θ)
questions.explanation: Differentiating d sin(θ) = mλ with respect to λ yields d cos(θ) dθ = m dλ, giving D = dθ/dλ = m / (d cos θ).

questions.question: If screen distance L is increased from 1.0 m to 2.0 m, how does the fringe displacement y change on the screen?
options: Displacement y doubles (y = L · tan θ)
questions.answer: Displacement y doubles (y = L · tan θ)
questions.correct_option: Displacement y doubles (y = L · tan θ)
questions.explanation: From geometry, tan(θ) = y / L, so y = L tan(θ). Linear fringe separation scales in direct proportion to screen distance L.

questions.question: What class of diffraction occurs when incident wavefronts are plane and observed at infinity (or focused by a lens)?
questions.answer: Fraunhofer diffraction
questions.correct_option: Fraunhofer diffraction
questions.explanation: Fraunhofer diffraction occurs in the far-field regime where both the incoming and outgoing wavefronts are planar.

questions.question: The chromatic resolving power of a diffraction grating is given by:
questions.answer: R = λ / Δλ = m · N_total
questions.correct_option: R = λ / Δλ = m · N_total
questions.explanation: By Rayleigh's criterion, two spectral lines are resolved when their angular separation matches half-width: R = λ/Δλ = m · N_total.

questions.question: What governs the sharpness and intensity of principal maxima in an N-slit diffraction grating?
options: Peak intensity is proportional to N² and angular width is inversely proportional to N
Peak intensity is proportional to N and width is independent of N
Peak intensity decreases as N increases
Sharpness is determined exclusively by screen distance
questions.answer: Peak intensity is proportional to N² and angular width is inversely proportional to N
questions.correct_option: Peak intensity is proportional to N² and angular width is inversely proportional to N
questions.explanation: Coherent constructive addition of N waves yields amplitude N · A₀ and intensity N² · I₀, while the width of the principal maximum narrows as 1/N.

questions.question: How many secondary minima exist between two adjacent principal maxima in an N-slit grating?
questions.answer: N - 1 minima
questions.correct_option: N - 1 minima
questions.explanation: Between consecutive principal maxima, the phase difference traverses 2π, encountering N - 1 zero-amplitude nodes (minima) and N - 2 secondary maxima.

questions.question: A laser with wavelength 500 nm strikes a grating with slit spacing d = 2.0 μm. What is sin(θ) for the first-order beam?
What is the optical path difference between rays from adjacent slits for the second-order maximum (m = 2)?
questions.answer: 2λ
questions.correct_option: 2λ
questions.explanation: For the m-th principal maximum, the path difference Δx = d sin(θ) must equal exactly mλ = 2λ.

questions.question: What causes a missing order (absent spectrum) in a diffraction grating pattern?
options: A principal interference maximum coincides with a single-slit diffraction minimum
The incident beam is polarized at Brewster's angle
The wavelength exceeds the physical size of the grating
Total internal reflection inside the glass substrate
questions.answer: A principal interference maximum coincides with a single-slit diffraction minimum
questions.correct_option: A principal interference maximum coincides with a single-slit diffraction minimum
questions.explanation: When the condition for a grating maximum (d sin θ = mλ) coincides with a single-slit diffraction zero (a sin θ = pλ), the intensity envelope is zero, extinguishing the order.

questions.question: Why do higher order spectra (e.g. m = 2 and m = 3) sometimes overlap when using polychromatic light?
options: Because m₁ · λ₁ can equal m₂ · λ₂ at identical diffraction angles θ
Because the grating heats up under laser irradiance
Because transverse magnetic modes cancel each other
Because light slows down inside the air gap
questions.answer: Because m₁ · λ₁ can equal m₂ · λ₂ at identical diffraction angles θ
questions.correct_option: Because m₁ · λ₁ can equal m₂ · λ₂ at identical diffraction angles θ
questions.explanation: Overlap occurs when 2 · λ_red (e.g., 2 × 700 = 1400 nm) exceeds 3 · λ_violet (3 × 400 = 1200 nm), placing different orders at overlapping angles.

questions.question: Why is a transmission diffraction grating widely preferred over a prism in quantitative spectrometry?
options: Gratings provide higher resolving power and linear angular dispersion
Gratings require no light source to operate
questions.answer: Gratings provide higher resolving power and linear angular dispersion
questions.correct_option: Gratings provide higher resolving power and linear angular dispersion
questions.explanation: Diffraction gratings yield much higher resolving power R and approximately linear dispersion dθ/dλ, making precise wavelength determination straightforward.

questions.question: What is the condition for missing spectra (absent orders) in a diffraction grating with slit width a and slit separation d?
options: d / a = m / p (where m is grating order and p is single-slit minimum order)
questions.answer: d / a = m / p (where m is grating order and p is single-slit minimum order)
questions.correct_option: d / a = m / p (where m is grating order and p is single-slit minimum order)
questions.explanation: When a principal interference maximum coincides with a single-slit diffraction minimum (d sin θ = mλ and a sin θ = pλ), the overall intensity vanishes, creating an absent order.

questions.question: If a transmission grating has slit width a = 2.0 μm and slit spacing d = 4.0 μm, which interference orders will be absent?
questions.answer: Even orders: m = 2, 4, 6, 8...
questions.correct_option: Even orders: m = 2, 4, 6, 8...
questions.explanation: d / a = 4.0 / 2.0 = 2. Therefore m = 2p, meaning all even orders (2, 4, 6...) coincide with single-slit diffraction zeros and disappear.

questions.question: What is the chromatic resolving power R of a diffraction grating defined as?
questions.answer: R = λ / Δλ = m · N_total
questions.correct_option: R = λ / Δλ = m · N_total
questions.explanation: By Rayleigh criterion, two spectral lines of wavelength difference Δλ are just resolved when R = λ / Δλ = m · N_total, where N_total is the total illuminated rulings.

questions.question: If a diffraction grating with 600 lines/mm is illuminated over a width of 20 mm, what is the total number of rulings N_total?
questions.answer: 12,000 lines
questions.correct_option: 12,000 lines
questions.explanation: N_total = (600 lines/mm) × (20 mm) = 12,000 rulings.

questions.question: For N_total = 12,000 rulings, what is the theoretical resolving power in the second order (m = 2)?
With a resolving power of R = 24,000 at λ = 600 nm, what is the smallest resolvable wavelength difference Δλ?
How does the angular dispersion D = dθ / dλ vary with the diffraction order m?
options: D is directly proportional to m (higher orders have wider spectral dispersion)
D is inversely proportional to m
D is completely independent of m
D approaches zero at higher orders
questions.answer: D is directly proportional to m (higher orders have wider spectral dispersion)
questions.correct_option: D is directly proportional to m (higher orders have wider spectral dispersion)
questions.explanation: Differentiating the grating equation gives D = dθ / dλ = m / (d cos θ). As m increases, angular dispersion increases proportionally.

questions.question: If light strikes a diffraction grating at an angle of incidence i, what is the modified grating equation?
options: d · (sin i + sin θ) = m · λ
d · (cos i + cos θ) = m · λ
questions.answer: d · (sin i + sin θ) = m · λ
questions.correct_option: d · (sin i + sin θ) = m · λ
questions.explanation: For oblique incidence, the total path difference across adjacent slits includes both incident and diffracted segments: d(sin i + sin θ) = mλ.

questions.question: Why do principal interference maxima become much sharper and brighter as the number of illuminated slits N increases?
options: Because destructive interference occurs at virtually all non-principal angles and peak intensity scales as N²
Because light travels faster through more slits
Because the wavelength of laser light decreases
Because the grating absorbs less thermal energy
questions.answer: Because destructive interference occurs at virtually all non-principal angles and peak intensity scales as N²
questions.correct_option: Because destructive interference occurs at virtually all non-principal angles and peak intensity scales as N²
questions.explanation: For N coherent in-phase wavelets, constructive amplitude is N · A₀ so peak intensity scales as I ∝ N², while angular half-width narrows as Δθ ∝ 1/N.

questions.question: In an N-slit diffraction grating, how many secondary minima exist between any two consecutive principal maxima?
questions.answer: (N − 1) minima
questions.correct_option: (N − 1) minima
questions.explanation: The interference term sin²(Nβ/2) / sin²(β/2) equals zero when Nβ/2 = pπ (with p not a multiple of N), yielding exactly (N - 1) minima.

questions.question: In an N-slit diffraction grating, how many secondary maxima exist between adjacent principal maxima?
questions.answer: (N − 2) secondary maxima
questions.correct_option: (N − 2) secondary maxima
questions.explanation: Between the (N - 1) secondary minima lie exactly (N - 2) weak secondary maxima whose intensities are negligible for large N.

questions.question: A diffraction grating has 1000 lines/mm. What is the maximum theoretical diffraction order for green laser light (λ = 500 nm)?
questions.answer: m_max = 2
questions.correct_option: m_max = 2

questions.question: What is the phase difference δ between wavelets diffracted at angle θ from adjacent slits separated by distance d?
questions.answer: δ = (2π / λ) · d · sin(θ)
questions.correct_option: δ = (2π / λ) · d · sin(θ)
questions.explanation: Phase difference δ = k · Δx = (2π / λ) · (d sin θ).

questions.question: What are Rowland's ghosts in ruled mechanical diffraction gratings?
options: Spurious spectral lines caused by periodic pitch errors in ruling engine drive screws
Optical reflections from the glass rear boundary
Fluorescence emission lines from diamond stylus wear
Second-order diffraction from ambient room illumination
questions.answer: Spurious spectral lines caused by periodic pitch errors in ruling engine drive screws
questions.correct_option: Spurious spectral lines caused by periodic pitch errors in ruling engine drive screws
questions.explanation: Periodic mechanical imperfections in the ruling screw produce systematic phase modulation, creating faint symmetrical ghost lines flanking principal lines.

questions.question: What is a blazed grating?
options: A grating with angled grooves designed to concentrate optical power into a specific diffraction order
A grating heated to high temperatures during fabrication
A grating coated with absorbing black paint
A transmission grating with non-parallel slits
questions.answer: A grating with angled grooves designed to concentrate optical power into a specific diffraction order
questions.correct_option: A grating with angled grooves designed to concentrate optical power into a specific diffraction order
questions.explanation: Blazing shifts the single-slit specular reflection envelope to match a chosen diffraction order, dramatically increasing diffraction efficiency at that blaze wavelength.

questions.question: What is the Littrow configuration in a spectrometer?
options: An optical geometry where the diffracted beam reflects back along the incident beam path (θ = i)
A geometry where light passes through two consecutive gratings
A setup using a cylindrical lens to collimate laser beams
A detector configuration without any focusing optics
questions.answer: An optical geometry where the diffracted beam reflects back along the incident beam path (θ = i)
questions.correct_option: An optical geometry where the diffracted beam reflects back along the incident beam path (θ = i)
questions.explanation: In the Littrow mount, θ = i so the grating equation simplifies to 2d sin θ = mλ, maximizing blaze efficiency and optical compactness.

questions.question: If a red laser (λ = 650 nm) is swapped for a violet laser (λ = 405 nm), what happens to the fringe pattern on the screen?
options: The diffracted spots move closer to the central zeroth-order spot
The diffracted spots move farther outward
questions.answer: The diffracted spots move closer to the central zeroth-order spot
questions.correct_option: The diffracted spots move closer to the central zeroth-order spot
questions.explanation: Since sin θ = mλ / d, a shorter wavelength produces smaller diffraction angles θ, contracting the fringe pattern toward center.

questions.question: If the grating-to-screen distance L is doubled, what happens to the physical distance y between the m = 0 and m = 1 spots?
options: The separation distance y approximately doubles
The separation distance y is halved
The separation distance y increases fourfold
The separation distance y remains unchanged
questions.answer: The separation distance y approximately doubles
questions.correct_option: The separation distance y approximately doubles
questions.explanation: For small angles, y ≈ L · tan(θ) ≈ L · θ. Doubling screen distance L directly doubles spot displacement y.

questions.question: What happens to the diffraction angles if an entire grating experiment is submerged in water (n = 1.33)?
options: Diffraction angles decrease because effective wavelength decreases (λ_med = λ / n)
The diffraction angles remain exactly the same
Diffraction completely ceases in liquid media
questions.answer: Diffraction angles decrease because effective wavelength decreases (λ_med = λ / n)
questions.correct_option: Diffraction angles decrease because effective wavelength decreases (λ_med = λ / n)
questions.explanation: In a dielectric medium of refractive index n, the wavelength shortens to λ / n, causing smaller diffraction angles via d sin θ = m(λ/n).

questions.question: Why does an atomic gas discharge tube produce discrete sharp spectral lines through a diffraction grating?
options: Because atoms emit photons at quantized discrete transition wavelengths ΔE = hc / λ
Because the grating filters out continuous frequencies
Because gas atoms absorb all odd orders
Because of acoustic Doppler resonance inside the tube
questions.answer: Because atoms emit photons at quantized discrete transition wavelengths ΔE = hc / λ
questions.correct_option: Because atoms emit photons at quantized discrete transition wavelengths ΔE = hc / λ
questions.explanation: Electronic transitions between quantized energy levels produce monochromatic photons at discrete wavelengths, each diffracted into distinct lines.

questions.question: What are the characteristic yellow doublet wavelengths of a low-pressure Sodium (Na) laboratory lamp?
questions.answer: 589.0 nm (D₂) and 589.6 nm (D₁)
questions.correct_option: 589.0 nm (D₂) and 589.6 nm (D₁)
questions.explanation: The Sodium doublet originates from 3p → 3s fine-structure transitions with wavelengths 589.0 nm and 589.6 nm separated by Δλ = 0.6 nm.

questions.question: What minimum resolving power R is required to clearly separate the Sodium doublet (589.0 nm and 589.6 nm)?
questions.explanation: R = λ_avg / Δλ = 589.3 nm / 0.6 nm ≈ 982. A grating needs at least ~982 total rulings in the first order to resolve them.

questions.question: Can a diffraction grating with N_total = 500 total rulings resolve the Sodium doublet in the first order (m = 1)?
options: No, because R = 1 × 500 = 500, which is less than the required 982
Yes, any grating can resolve the doublet
No, Sodium light cannot be diffracted by gratings
questions.answer: No, because R = 1 × 500 = 500, which is less than the required 982
questions.correct_option: No, because R = 1 × 500 = 500, which is less than the required 982
questions.explanation: In order m = 1, R = 500 < 982, so Rayleigh criterion is not met and the two lines blur together.

questions.question: What is the key structural difference between a transmission grating and a reflection grating?
options: Transmission gratings transmit diffracted light through transparent slits; reflection gratings reflect light from mirrored facets
Transmission gratings have only two slits
questions.answer: Transmission gratings transmit diffracted light through transparent slits; reflection gratings reflect light from mirrored facets
questions.correct_option: Transmission gratings transmit diffracted light through transparent slits; reflection gratings reflect light from mirrored facets
questions.explanation: Transmission gratings rely on periodic transmissive apertures; reflection gratings use periodic mirrored facets etched into a substrate.

questions.question: If a transmission grating has 1200 lines/mm, what is its slit spacing d in nanometers?
What is the diffraction angle θ for m = 1 with λ = 500 nm and d = 2000 nm?
In Fraunhofer multi-slit diffraction, what optical function does a collimating lens serve before the grating?
options: It converts diverging spherical rays into parallel planar wavefronts
It focuses diffracted light onto the sensor
questions.answer: It converts diverging spherical rays into parallel planar wavefronts
questions.correct_option: It converts diverging spherical rays into parallel planar wavefronts
questions.explanation: Fraunhofer diffraction strictly requires planar wavefront incidence, achieved by placing the point source at the focal point of a collimator lens.

questions.question: What governs the relative intensity envelope of different diffraction orders in a plane grating?
options: The single-slit diffraction factor [sin(α)/α]² where α = (π a sin θ) / λ
The thickness of the glass substrate only
The focal length of the telescope
The temperature of the laser diode
questions.answer: The single-slit diffraction factor [sin(α)/α]² where α = (π a sin θ) / λ
questions.correct_option: The single-slit diffraction factor [sin(α)/α]² where α = (π a sin θ) / λ
questions.explanation: The total intensity is the product of multi-slit interference and single-slit diffraction: I(θ) = I₀ · [sin(α)/α]² · [sin(Nβ)/sin(β)]².

questions.question: Why are holographic gratings often superior to mechanically ruled gratings in high-precision spectroscopy?
options: They are produced via laser interference fringes, eliminating mechanical ruling errors and ghost lines
They do not require optical alignment
They can amplify light like a laser amplifier
questions.answer: They are produced via laser interference fringes, eliminating mechanical ruling errors and ghost lines
questions.correct_option: They are produced via laser interference fringes, eliminating mechanical ruling errors and ghost lines
questions.explanation: Holographic fabrication records sinusoidal optical interference fringes onto photoresist, virtually eliminating periodic mechanical errors and stray light ghosts.

questions.question: What is the physical principle underlying the determination of laser wavelength using a transmission grating in this experiment?
options: Measuring the fringe position y and bench distance L gives θ = arctan(y/L), enabling calculation via λ = (d · sin θ) / m
Measuring the heat absorbed by the grating screen
Measuring the time of flight of laser photons
Detecting the Doppler redshift of laser light
questions.answer: Measuring the fringe position y and bench distance L gives θ = arctan(y/L), enabling calculation via λ = (d · sin θ) / m
questions.correct_option: Measuring the fringe position y and bench distance L gives θ = arctan(y/L), enabling calculation via λ = (d · sin θ) / m
questions.explanation: By geometry, tan θ = y / L. Substituting θ into the grating equation d sin θ = mλ yields the unknown laser wavelength with high precision.
